common.name: Name
settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Preferences stored in the configuration file. General covers appearance, the configuration file and the language; Providers covers subscription accounts and the providers pi knows; MCP covers the servers pi can use as tools.
settings.general.appearance.description: Theme used across the whole app.
settings.general.chat.description: How the conversation is displayed and how prompts are sent.
settings.general.showReasoning.descripti: Show the reasoning the agent produces above each answer. When off, it is never rendered.
settings.general.queueMessages.descripti: While the agent is working, sending keeps the prompt in a queue for this session and it is sent when the current turn ends.
settings.general.language.description: Language of the interface. It applies immediately.
settings.general.tools.description: Which tools the tools panel offers. Terminal and Browser are off by default because they run code.
settings.general.tools.files.description: Browse the workspace and preview a file in the same tab.
settings.general.tools.changes.descripti: Review the working tree and read the diff of each file.
settings.general.tools.terminal.descript: A real shell in the workspace, opened only while its tab is active.
settings.general.tools.terminal.warning: The terminal runs whatever you type, with your user's permissions.
settings.general.tools.browser.descripti: Shows what the agent does in a dedicated browser.
settings.general.tools.browser.warning: The browser drives a real Chromium instance the agent can navigate and act in.
settings.providers.title: Providers
settings.providers.description: Providers pi knows. The active one is the provider the next session starts with.
settings.providers.empty: pi has no providers configured yet.
settings.providers.edit.title: Edit {name}
settings.providers.edit.description: The ID, base URL and model count are read from pi's configuration file; its models are edited below.
settings.providers.apiKey.label: API key for {id}
settings.providers.apiKey.description: Stored as plain text in pi's configuration file.
settings.providers.remove.title: Remove provider?
settings.providers.remove.description: Remove {id} from your provider configuration? The entry is deleted from the configuration file (a backup is kept).
settings.providers.remove.missing: That provider is no longer in the configuration file.
settings.providers.remove.activeWarning: The active provider was removed and none are left; the configured provider stays as it was.
settings.providers.custom.title: Add provider
settings.providers.custom.description: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It is saved to pi's own provider configuration.
settings.providers.custom.preset.descrip: Fills the ID, name and base URL once; every field stays editable afterwards.
settings.providers.custom.id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 32 characters.
settings.providers.custom.name: Name
settings.providers.custom.name.descripti: Optional. The ID is shown while it is empty.
settings.providers.custom.baseUrl.descri: The API root, for example https://api.example.com/v1.
settings.providers.custom.apiKey.descrip: Stored as plain text in pi's configuration file.
settings.providers.custom.selectModels: Discover the endpoint's models to pick them.
settings.providers.custom.required: ID, base URL and API key are required.
settings.providers.modelsEditor.heading: Models
settings.providers.modelsEditor.descript: Context, limits, costs and input modalities of this provider's models. Saves are written to pi's configuration file with a backup.
settings.providers.modelsEditor.catalogH: These models come from the provider's published catalogue. pi manages them, so they are read-only here.
settings.providers.modelsEditor.empty: This provider has no models in the configuration file.
settings.providers.modelsEditor.name: Name
settings.providers.modelsEditor.invalidN: Limits and costs must be numbers; leave them empty to keep the stored value.
settings.providers.modelsEditor.remove.d: Remove {modelId} from {provider}? The entry is deleted from the configuration file (a backup is kept).
settings.providers.modelsEditor.discover: Asks the provider's endpoint for its model list, using the base URL and API key from the configuration file. Only models that are not configured yet are offered, so nothing already here is replaced.
Every model the endpoint returned is already configured.
settings.accounts.title: Subscription accounts
settings.accounts.description: Sign in with a subscription so pi can use these providers. Only subscription providers are listed here; every other endpoint belongs to the Providers list. pi stores the credentials.
settings.accounts.signOut.title: Sign out?
settings.accounts.signOut.description: pi deletes the stored credential for {id}. You can sign in again at any time; the provider's api key in the configuration file is not touched.
settings.accounts.signOut.timeout: pi did not answer in time; the account state was read again.
settings.accounts.signOut.failed: pi could not sign out (exit code {code}).
settings.accounts.login.openManually: The browser could not open the link. It is under “Trouble signing in?”.
settings.accounts.login.openFailed: The browser could not be opened. Copy the link and open it manually.
settings.accounts.login.callbackHint: The browser finishes the sign-in on its own when the callback on 127.0.0.1 receives the answer; the field below is only needed if it hands you a code.
settings.accounts.login.notAccepted: pi is no longer waiting for a code; start the sign-in again.
sidebar.empty: No workspaces yet — add a folder with the folder button.
sidebar.duplicatePath: That workspace path is already in the list.
workspace.editDescription: Renaming and deleting a workspace land in the next unit. This is what the store holds today.
session.delete.title: Delete this session?
session.delete.description: Its transcript moves to the archive folder and it disappears from the list.
chat.reasoning.label: Reasoning
chat.code.label: code
chat.error.label: Error
chat.noWorkspaceHint: No workspace selected — add or pick one in the sidebar.
chat.errors.noWorkspace: Select a workspace before sending a prompt.
chat.composer.placeholder: Describe what you want to build, / commands, @ files or sessions
chat.queue.heading: Queued ({count})
settings.mcp.title: MCP servers
settings.mcp.description: Servers pi can use as tools, read from pi's own configuration. Sign in here when a server asks for it.
settings.mcp.signOut.title: Sign out of this server?
settings.mcp.signOut.description: Sign out of {name}? pi deletes the OAuth credentials it stored for this server; the entry stays in the configuration.
settings.mcp.remove.title: Remove server?
settings.mcp.remove.description: Remove {name} from the {scope} MCP configuration? The entry is deleted from the file; pi keeps any credentials it stored.
settings.mcp.login.openManually: Could not open the browser. Open the URL from the details below.
settings.mcp.login.openFailed: The browser did not open. Copy the URL above.
settings.mcp.login.redirectHint: If the browser runs on another machine, paste the redirected URL here.
settings.mcp.login.notAccepted: The sign-in is no longer waiting for input.
settings.mcp.form.title: Add an MCP server
settings.mcp.form.description: The entry is written to pi's MCP configuration. Nothing is downloaded or installed.
settings.mcp.form.catalog.title: From the catalogue
settings.mcp.form.catalog.description: Templates that only fill this form. Nothing is installed and nothing is sent until you save.
settings.mcp.form.name: Name
settings.mcp.form.name.description: Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` only, up to 64 characters.
settings.mcp.form.nameInvalid: Use only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` (1-64 characters).
settings.mcp.form.scope.description: Global is shared by every workspace; project lives in this workspace's `.pi/mcp.json` and is read only in a trusted project.
settings.mcp.form.transport.description: stdio runs a local process; http connects to a remote endpoint.
settings.mcp.form.command.description: One executable, not a shell string. The arguments go below.
settings.mcp.form.commandInvalid: One executable with no spaces. Put the arguments in the field below.
settings.mcp.form.urlInvalid: Use an absolute http:// or https:// URL.
settings.mcp.form.env.description: Passed to the process. Values may use ${NAME} or !command.
settings.mcp.form.headers.description: Sent with every request. Values may use ${NAME} or !command.
settings.mcp.form.bearerEnvVar.descripti: Optional. pi sends Authorization: Bearer ${NAME} using the variable with this name.
settings.mcp.form.bearerEnvVarInvalid: Use a variable name: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit.
settings.mcp.form.pairKeyMissing: Every row with a value needs a name.
settings.mcp.form.required: Fill the required fields to save.
settings.mcp.files.title: Configuration files
settings.mcp.files.description: Where pi keeps these entries. Nabla reads them through pi and never edits them by hand.
settings.mcp.form.pairKeyInvalid: A name cannot contain `=` or spaces.
tools.title: Tools
tools.tabs.empty: No tab is open. Use + to open one.
tools.tabs.noTools: No tool is enabled. Turn one on in Settings → Tools.
tools.dock.chooseFolder: Choose the folder this pane shows
tools.files.label: Files
tools.files.noWorkspace: Select a workspace to browse its files.
tools.preview.binary: Binary file: there is nothing to preview.
tools.changes.label: Changes
tools.changes.noWorkspace: Select a workspace to see its changes.
tools.changes.error: Could not read the working tree: {message}
tools.changes.diffEmpty: This file has no textual differences.
tools.terminal.label: Terminal
tools.terminal.noWorkspace: Select a workspace to open a shell in it.
tools.browser.label: Browser
tools.browser.hint: Type an http or https address and press Enter.
tools.browser.urlInvalid: Only http and https addresses can be opened here.
tools.browser.createError: Could not open the browser view: {message}
tools.browser.controlError: Could not run that action in the page: {message}
tools.browser.layoutError: Could not place the browser view: {message}
tools.browser.syncError: The address bar cannot follow the page: {message}
tools.browser.agentNote: The agent drives this view through the nabla-browser MCP tools: it navigates, reads and clicks in the page you are looking at.
